solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Easy task? Part of it could be a piece of cake

definitions.meaning: something that is no trouble at all, a doddle

definitions.text: Part of it could be a piece of cake
definitions.meaning: an outdoor meal eaten from a hamper, which might well include a slice of cake

explanation.surface: Someone muses that an easy job, like a piece of cake, is only part of the story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A piece of cake' is the idiom for an easy task, steering you to think both halves mean the same; the second is a literal slice of cake packed for an outing.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiomatically an effortless job is called this; literally it is an alfresco meal where cake may be served.

clue.text: Unable to move under white blanket

definitions.meaning: stuck, trapped and unable to get out
covered over by a thick fall of snow

explanation.surface: Someone lies stuck beneath a white bedcover, unable to get up.
explanation.walkthrough: The white blanket reads as bedding, but it is a fall of snow; being trapped at home by it is the first sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means confined indoors by heavy snowfall, and also literally buried beneath snow.

clue.text: Fish from front or stern of dinghy

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter, here of dinghy
the stern is the back of a boat, so the closing letter of dinghy

explanation.surface: An angler pulls a fish over the bow or the back of a small boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'front' takes the D at the start of dinghy and 'stern of' its final Y; the word 'or' sits between them as written.
explanation.definitionFit: A John Dory is an edible sea fish, often called simply by its surname.

clue.text: Duke attached to court in deal, for example

indicators.note: the duke's letter is fastened onto the end of the courting word

parts.note: to court someone is to woo them

explanation.surface: A duke joins a royal court as part of some business deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deal' looks like a bargain but is the timber: deal is pine or fir planking.
explanation.definitionFit: Deal is a kind of softwood timber, so it is an example of this material.

clue.text: Ornamental shrub is feature of cathedral area

parts.note: a spire is the tall pointed tower on many cathedrals

explanation.surface: A decorative bush turns out to be a highlight of the cathedral grounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiraea or spirea is a garden bush grown for its sprays of small white or pink flowers.

clue.text: Unable to deliver speech in exceptionally low dress

indicators.note: taken as out of the ordinary, it tells us the letters of the next two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is struck dumb by an unusually low-cut dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exceptionally' seems to describe how low the dress is, but it signals rearranging LOW DRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Being speechless or silent means having no words to say.

clue.text: Kind of rock wayward genius has put in ring

indicators.note: the ring shape is placed inside the jumbled letters
wayward means going astray, so the letters of genius wander into a new order

parts.note: a ring is round like the letter O

explanation.surface: A rebellious genius has set a stone into a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wayward' rearranges GENIUS to IGNEUS, and 'has put in' places O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock formed from cooled molten magma, such as granite or basalt, is one of the main geological classes.

clue.text: Place with company, finally, as regular partner

parts.note: stead means place, as in 'in his stead'

indicators.note: takes only the closing letter of the word company

explanation.surface: Someone finally finds a place among company as a steady partner.
explanation.definitionFit: A boyfriend or girlfriend one goes out with regularly is informally called this.

clue.text: Somehow, is crop circle a sign?

indicators.note: suggests the letters are put together in some other way, i.e. rearranged

parts.note: a circle is shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A puzzled observer wonders whether a crop circle is a portent.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening word rearranges IS CROP into SCORPI, then O, shaped like a circle, ends it.
explanation.definitionFit: The scorpion is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Bird appearing as one's sitting in hide

indicators.note: the pair of letters is seated inside the other word

parts.note: an animal's hide is its skin
one's is I'S, written as IS

explanation.surface: A bird watcher's quarry appears as someone sits in a bird hide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hide' looks like a birdwatching shelter but is the skin; I (one) plus 'S sit inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A small yellow-green finch of conifer woods is a well-known songbird.

clue.text: United duo having just achieved goal in match?

definitions.text: United duo having just achieved goal in match?

parts.words: United duo having just achieved goal in match?
parts.note: a football-sounding picture of two players, but really a couple just joined in marriage

explanation.surface: Two Manchester United players celebrate a goal they have just scored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'United' and 'goal in match' suggest football; here the match is a marriage and the united duo a couple fresh from the ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple who have only recently married have just reached the aim of their union.

clue.text: Daughter and a friend, ignoring the odds, took on challenge

indicators.note: skips the first, third and fifth letters of friend, keeping the even ones

explanation.surface: A daughter and her friend, against the odds, accepted a dare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring the odds' sounds like bravery but takes R, E, D from friend.
explanation.definitionFit: To have ventured or been bold enough to do something is to have risen to a challenge.

clue.text: Method of paying, initially, that could be catch

definitions.meaning: initials of cash on delivery, a way of settling a bill
a fish an angler might land

explanation.surface: A shopper wonders whether paying on delivery hides a catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' tells you the payment method is given by its initials; 'catch' looks like a snag but is a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Cash on delivery is abbreviated this way, and it is also a common food fish.

clue.text: Its consumers are celebrating achievement of union

definitions.text: Its consumers are celebrating achievement of union

parts.words: Its consumers are celebrating achievement of union
parts.note: the guests eating it are toasting a couple who have just married, not a trade union win

explanation.surface: Union members celebrate a hard-won victory together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union' suggests organised labour; the union is a marriage and the consumers are guests at the reception.
explanation.definitionFit: The tiered confection served at a reception is eaten by guests marking a marriage.

clue.text: Practice a craft, as setter and solvers have stated

indicators.note: spoken out loud, signalling a word that sounds like another

parts.note: setter and solvers together are 'we', so they have is WE'VE

explanation.surface: A crossword setter and their solvers declare they practise a craft.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter plus solvers say 'we've', which sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Interlacing threads on a loom is a traditional handicraft.

clue.text: Casual garments, we hear — they're passed on by parents

indicators.note: tells us to go by sound rather than spelling

parts.note: jeans are casual denim trousers

explanation.surface: Hand-me-down casual clothes are passed from parents to children.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests handed-down jeans; the inheritance is biological.
explanation.definitionFit: Units of heredity are inherited by children from their mother and father.

clue.text: Finishes off any new ale — one way to work on glass

definitions.text: one way to work on glass

indicators.note: each of the three words loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone polishes off any new ale on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finishes off' sounds like drinking up, but it removes the last letter of each word: Y, W and E, leaving AN, NE, AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Heating glass and cooling it slowly toughens it, a standard technique in glassmaking.

clue.text: Including account in financial check, said why that's bold

indicators.note: the abbreviation for account is placed within the financial check

parts.note: an audit is an inspection of accounts

indicators.note: spoken aloud, so a word is replaced by a letter that sounds the same

parts.note: the word why, whose sound is that of the letter Y

explanation.surface: An auditor checks the accounts and asks why something is so daring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Including' and 'said' are the two indicators; the definition 'that's bold' means the quality a bold act shows, so it fits a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Boldness or daring cheek is the quality shown by what is bold, so 'that's bold' describes it.

clue.text: Records a pair of names, too — endlessly together

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for name, so two of them make NN

indicators.note: the last letter is cut off the word for too

parts.note: also means too

explanation.surface: Someone records two names together, apparently forever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' looks like it means forever but trims ALSO to ALS.
explanation.definitionFit: Year-by-year historical chronicles are written records of events.

clue.text: Transformed art tome with old representation of Cupid

indicators.note: changed in form, so the letters of art tome are rearranged

explanation.surface: An old art book is changed to include a picture of Cupid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transformed' rearranges ART TOME to AMORETT, then O follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A cherub or little cupid figure in Renaissance art is called by this Italian term.

clue.text: Really liked a party on extreme left

parts.note: a do is a party
Red describes a communist or radical left-winger

explanation.surface: Someone loved a party on the far left of politics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extreme left' seems to mean a position, but a far-left radical is a Red.
explanation.definitionFit: To have loved or worshipped something is to have liked it very much.

clue.text: Cause of tears known to the cognoscenti?

definitions.meaning: the vegetable that makes your eyes water when you chop it
experts are said to know their ..., i.e. to know their subject well

explanation.surface: Someone asks what makes people cry that only the experts would know.
explanation.walkthrough: The British idiom 'to know your onions' means to be knowledgeable, so experts know them.
explanation.definitionFit: The pungent bulbs make cooks weep, and the idiom about expertise gives the second sense.

clue.text: They extend a line — casts twice end badly

indicators.note: suggests something done wrongly, so the letters get mixed up
the word end is used two times

explanation.surface: An angler whose casts both end badly extends the fishing line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice' doubles END; 'badly' rearranges CASTS ENDEND.
explanation.definitionFit: Children and grandchildren continue a family lineage into later generations.

clue.text: Does some gardening work in suit

definitions.meaning: one of the four suits of playing cards

explanation.surface: Someone does a bit of gardening while wearing a suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' looks like clothing but is a suit of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Digging uses a long-handled tool, and the black card suit is named after it.

clue.text: Original piece of art framed in fine 4

definitions.note: refers to the answer to 4 down, a material

indicators.note: the letter from art sits inside the other word like a picture in a frame

parts.note: OK means fine

indicators.note: the opening letter of art

explanation.surface: An original work of art is set in a fine wooden frame.
explanation.walkthrough: '4' is the answer to 4 Down; 'framed in' puts A (from art) inside OK.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardwood tree whose timber is prized is a classic example of the material named at 4.

clue.text: Satisfied with endless show of affection? That's fate

indicators.note: the satisfied word is joined on after the shortened kiss
the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a kiss is a show of affection
a demand that is met has been satisfied

explanation.surface: Someone content with an endless display of love accepts it as destiny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims KISS to KIS.
explanation.definitionFit: This Turkish-derived word means destiny or predetermined fortune.

clue.text: For example, working with 4 boats

definitions.meaning: a skill such as working with timber, a handicraft

explanation.surface: Working with timber, for example, gives you boats.
explanation.walkthrough: '4' is the answer to 4 Down; woodwork is a skilled trade.
explanation.definitionFit: A handiwork skill such as joinery is a trade, and vessels or boats are also called this.

clue.text: Timber used in the afterdeck, being extremely selective

indicators.note: only the extreme letters, first and last, of each word are chosen

explanation.surface: Choosy shipbuilders use only one particular timber for the rear deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being extremely selective' picks the ends of THE and AFTERDECK: TE and AK.
explanation.definitionFit: A durable tropical hardwood often used for boat decks.

clue.text: Desirable feature of house that's comprehended by groom, in essence

indicators.note: comprehended in its sense of contained or included, so the letters sit within the words

explanation.surface: An estate agent says the essential selling point is understood by any groom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comprehended' looks like understood but means contained.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaciousness is a quality homebuyers value in a property.

clue.text: Revered person adding line to acceptance speech

indicators.note: the line letter is put on after the vow

parts.note: 'I do' is what is said at a wedding to accept a partner

explanation.surface: An admired figure adds a line to their award acceptance speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'acceptance speech' suggests an awards ceremony; it is the wedding vow 'I do'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone worshipped or adored, like a pop star or an image of a god.

clue.text: Literary great, in time, was told about book

indicators.note: the word for was told goes around the letter for book

parts.note: heard means was told

explanation.surface: A great writer, in his day, was told about a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' places B inside HEARD to give HEBARD, after T. The Bard is Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare, the most celebrated English writer, is nicknamed this.

clue.text: Dog that is with novelist from same part of world

definitions.text: Dog that is with novelist from same part of world

parts.note: Sir Walter Scott, the Scottish author of Ivanhoe
IE is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A dog and a novelist turn out to share a homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: the terrier and Sir Walter Scott both come from Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish terrier, a breed from the same country as the author of Ivanhoe, is affectionately known by this short name.
